stages.label: Checking that your data structure is ready

researcher_status.plain_language_title: Some assay results belong to participants who are not in the participant file
researcher_status.plain_language_summary: 1 assay row(s) refer to 1 participant identifier(s) that do not appear in the participant file.
researcher_status.why_it_matters: Results that cannot be linked to a participant cannot be analysed, and may indicate that the two files come from different dataset versions.
researcher_status.next_action: Check that the participant and assay files are from the same dataset version. If an assay is a known exception, record it in the approved-exceptions list.
researcher_status.resolving_role: The data custodian or the person who prepared the data file.

findings.plain_language_title: Some assay results belong to participants who are not in the participant file
findings.plain_language_summary: 1 assay row(s) refer to 1 participant identifier(s) that do not appear in the participant file.
findings.why_it_matters: Results that cannot be linked to a participant cannot be analysed, and may indicate that the two files come from different dataset versions.
findings.next_action: Check that the participant and assay files are from the same dataset version. If an assay is a known exception, record it in the approved-exceptions list.
findings.resolving_role: The data custodian or the person who prepared the data file.

findings.plain_language_title: Some participants are missing required assay results
findings.plain_language_summary: 1 required assay result(s) are missing across 1 participant(s).
findings.why_it_matters: The approved plan expects every participant to have a result for each target in the panel. Missing rows change the sample size.
findings.next_action: Add the missing results, or record each missing result as an approved exception with the reason and who approved it.
findings.resolving_role: The data custodian or the person who prepared the data file.

findings.plain_language_summary: 1 participant-and-target combination(s) appear more than once in the assay file.
findings.why_it_matters: Duplicated rows would count a participant more than once. Whether repeat measurements are allowed is a decision for the research plan, not for the runner.
findings.next_action: Remove accidental duplicates. If repeat measurements are intended, the research plan must say how they are handled before the analysis can run.
